chunks: And it is narrated from Mismaʿ Abī Sayyār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I had entrusted a man with some wealth, but he denied it to me and swore concerning it to me. Then, after two years, he came to me with the wealth that I had entrusted to him, and said: This is your wealth, so take it. And these are four thousand dirhams that I earned as profit; they are yours along with your wealth. And put me in your absolution.

So I took the wealth from him, but I refused to take the profit from him. And I withheld the wealth that I had entrusted, and I refused to take it until I could seek your opinion. So what do you think?
He عليه السلام said: Take half of the profit and give him the other half, and absolve him, for this is a repentant man, and Allah

key_terms.اسْتَوْدَعْتُ: I entrusted property to someone as a deposit
key_terms.تَائِبٌ: one who has repented and returned from wrongdoing
key_terms.جَحَدَنِيهِ: he denied the entrusted property to me
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of absolution or release from claim
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or property being held in trust
key_terms.نِصْفَ الرِّبْحِ: half of the profit earned from the wealth

ai.seo_question: What should be done if someone denies a deposit, later repents, and returns it with profit?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a case of entrusted wealth that was denied and later returned with added profit after the custodian repented. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that half the profit be taken and half left for the repentant man, while also granting him absolution, reflecting both legal judgment and encouragement of tawbah.
